# Cheat Engine CLI

> Cheat Engine CLI (`cecli`) is an independent, JSON-first command-line interface with native macOS and Windows process-memory access plus remote administration and bounded debugger workflows through the upstream Cheat Engine `ceserver` protocol.

## Canonical sources

- [Product overview](https://chengyixu.github.io/cheat-engine-cli/): Definition, features, safety model, quick start, and FAQ.
- [简体中文 README](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli/blob/master/README.zh-CN.md): 中文产品介绍、安装、命令、安全模型和常见问题。
- [Source repository](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli): Code, tests, release artifacts, issues, and upstream history.
- [Command reference](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli/blob/master/docs/command-reference.md): Commands, flags, value types, examples, and exit codes.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli/blob/master/docs/architecture.md): Protocol reuse, stateless command model, scanner design, and current scope.
- [Security policy](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli/blob/master/SECURITY.md): Authorized-use expectations and reporting guidance.
- [Notices](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli/blob/master/NOTICE.md): Upstream attribution and licensing status.
- [Companion agent skill](https://github.com/chengyixu/cheat-engine-cli-skill): English and Simplified Chinese playbooks for authorized native and remote `cecli` workflows.

## Supported capabilities

- Native macOS and Windows process discovery, memory regions, reads, exact scans, and guarded writes with `--native`
- `ceserver` version and ABI discovery
- Process, module, and thread enumeration
- Thread suspend/resume counts during an active debug session
- Process architecture and memory region inspection
- Typed memory reads: signed/unsigned integers, floats, UTF-8, UTF-16LE, hex, base64
- Exact typed-value scans and byte-pattern scans with `??` wildcards
- Explicit confirmation-gated compatibility access to the patched server-side AOB packet
- Alignment, address range, protection, timeout, and result limits
- Memory write dry-run, explicit confirmation, and optional verification
- Memory allocation, free, and page-protection changes with explicit confirmation
- Target-side module loading and speed control with dry-run and confirmation
- Explicit-dlopen module loading and ceserver extension injection
- Server path and runtime option inspection with verified option changes
- Per-connection diagnostic naming and confirmation-gated remote server termination
- Remote filesystem list, stat, download, upload, mkdir, delete, chmod, pwd, and cd
- Named-pipe open/read/write/close and compressed ELF symbol listing
- Bounded debug-event traces with event limits, timeouts, and automatic continuation
- Active-session hardware breakpoint set/remove commands
- Raw thread-context export and confirmation-gated replacement with optional verification
- JSON-first output, structured stderr errors, stable exit codes, dotted field projection, and silent exit-code probes
- Typed command-specific help with defaults, enums, conditional constraints, and response-envelope schemas
- Catalog-derived nested Bash, Zsh, and Fish completions
- Embedded agent rules, skills, and local issue feedback

## Current limitations

- Native mode currently covers the core process-memory subset; modules, threads, debugger controls, remote administration, allocation, and protection changes require a remote `ceserver` endpoint.
- macOS native access requires a debugger-signed CLI and still cannot inspect SIP-protected processes; native Linux access is not implemented.
- Native architecture-aware register decoding is not implemented; thread contexts are returned as validated raw base64 blobs.
- Legacy duplicate packets are internal or superseded; upstream-defined but undispatched `CMD_STOPDEBUG`, `CMD_PTRACE_MMAP`, and `CMD_COMMANDLIST2` have no callable server handler.
- Independent project; not an official Cheat Engine release.
